- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model often overshoots; cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 5–10% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average before applying forecast adjustments.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >15% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean (last 18 days) unless sentiment strongly supports divergence.
- When sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
